concerns.text: Constitution Principle VI mandates validation against a 'small-scale physical deployment of 10–20 local machines'. Task T035a_Ci_Gate and T035a_Mock introduce a 'Mock Dataset' fallback for CI when physical hardware is unavailable. This silently relaxes the constitutional requirement that the simulation MUST be validated against real physical data to prevent circular predictions. A mock dataset cannot satisfy the 'Validation Independence' requirement of Principle VI.

FR-002 and SC-006 require capturing 'unmodeled variables' (thermal throttling, OS noise) and handling missing data by proceeding with 'reduced model complexity'. Task T014a states: 'If metrics are missing... log a WARNING and proceed; do NOT abort'. It fails to explicitly implement the logic to dynamically prune the regression formula (interaction terms) as mandated by SC-006, effectively weakening the acceptance criterion for handling missing non-critical variables.

FR-003 and US-1 require 'injecting controlled network impairments' (real latency/packet loss) to measure heterogeneity. Task T025b introduces a fallback to 'software-based latency simulation (using Python time.sleep())' if `tc` is unavailable. This relaxes the requirement for real network impairment injection, as software sleep loops do not replicate the packet loss/latency characteristics of a real Wi-Fi network, violating the semantic intent of the 'heterogeneity' variable in the regression model.

FR-005 explicitly requires 'multiple linear regression' outputting coefficients and R². While T030a implements MLR and T035b selects a model, the tasks do not clearly define how the 'sweet spot' hypothesis (SC-003) is measured if the GAM (non-linear) and MLR (linear) models produce conflicting results regarding the existence of an inflection point. This creates a semantic gap in the verification step for the primary research claim.
